subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, tool-calls, and token safety
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@nymble.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, tool-calls, and token safety

Hi Alex — great to meet you and demo the flow earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the PoC: 

1) SDK & auth: you mentioned wanting a token-per-endpoint approach for fine-grained throttling. For the PoC do you prefer:
   - short-lived API keys per service (we provide key rotation examples in the SDK), or
   - integration with your existing OAuth2 server (we have an example for token exchange + RBAC)?

2) Routing & fallbacks: we recommend setting an explicit route policy for high-priority calls (low-latency chat) vs batch reranks. Can you confirm which endpoints in your app are latency-sensitive vs background?

3) Structured output / tool-calls: you showed the calendar tool and the internal lookup. For the PoC we'll wire up Redwood function calls (tool-calling); would you like us to enforce a strict JSON schema for tool responses on success?

4) Request/response semantics: two quick asks that affect token accounting and streaming:
   - Are you expecting streaming partial replies for user-visible chat (yes/no)? If yes we will recommend the streaming SDK path and provide examples for streaming + retries.
   - Do you plan to use structured stop sequences (e.g. '###END') or rely on max_tokens truncation? We should pick one to avoid truncated JSON payloads from model responses.

I attached a lightweight PoC checklist and short SDK snippets for auth to help you choose. Next steps: if you can reply with your preference on (1) auth style and (4) streaming vs stop-sequence, we’ll produce a scoped PoC plan + rough capacity estimate by Friday.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx]
[Attachment: sdk-auth-snippets.md]

--
Note: their privacy team asked about token retention and reranker caching; Ben and Laura, I cc’d you for the technical follow-ups.
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@nymble.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, tool-calls, and token safety

Thanks Irene — a couple of implementation notes for Alex that will help the PoC move faster: 

- Auth: our SDK supports both short-lived API keys and OAuth token exchange. For per-endpoint throttling we typically issue scoped API keys using Redwood "subkeys" (example in sdk-auth-snippets.md). That avoids needing an OAuth flow during PoC.

- Streaming semantics: streaming is enabled at the client call level (stream=true). Important details:
  * Streaming sends delta tokens as events; token accounting is the same as completed responses.
  * If you use streaming + tool-calling, ensure the client can accept mid-stream tool-invocation events (we include a parser in the SDK).
  * For critical structured outputs, we prefer enforcing a trailing stop token (e.g., '###END') and validating the final JSON; streaming reduces perceived latency but increases the need for robust reassembly and checksum.

- Chat vs completions: Use the chat endpoint if you need turn-based system/user/assistant roles and tooling; completions endpoint is fine for single-shot prompts or rerank pipeline steps. For rerankers/embeddings: send candidate items as batch embeddings and call the reranker in a sync completion with max_tokens small to avoid long tails.

I'll paste a minimal code snippet below (see sdk-auth-snippets.md for full examples).

Ben
Senior Devtools, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex@nymble.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, tool-calls, and token safety

Irene/Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Auth: for speed of PoC we prefer scoped short-lived API keys (no OAuth for now). We'll want a migration path to our OAuth server later.

2) Latency-sensitive routes: chat endpoints for in-product assistant (sub-200ms target); background reranks and batch embeddings can be async.

3) Structured output: yes — we want strict JSON schema enforcement for tool outputs (calendar, lookup). Avoid relying on max_tokens to terminate JSON.

4) Streaming: we want streaming for the user-visible chat to improve perceived latency, but we acknowledge the need for reassembly. We'll use a trailing stop token '###END' for JSON tool responses and validate on the client. 

Additional note: our security lead asked whether Redwood persists any KV cache derived from user prompts; briefly — do you store KV cache or prefix caches by default? If so, can we opt-out for PII-sensitive conversations?

I'll attach a short doc with our latency targets and the list of endpoints we consider high-priority. Once you confirm the PoC plan we can schedule an engineering sync early next week.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Nymble AI
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@nymble.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, tool-calls, and token safety

Thanks Alex — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. Quick follow-ups and actions: 

- PoC scope: we will proceed with scoped short-lived API keys + examples for token rotation. We’ll include a migration note for OAuth later.

- Streaming + stop token: we’ll provide two client examples: (A) streaming chat with reassembly + validation against the trailing '###END' stop token, (B) non-streaming validated call that asserts schema before returning.

- KV/prefix cache: Redwood runtime caches KV for performance (prefix/KV cache for autoregressive decoding). We can disable caching per-route and mark caches as non-persistent for the PoC (opt-out available). I’ll include exact config keys in the PoC checklist.

Planned deliverables (by Friday):
  - PoC task list + success criteria (capacity, latency targets, schema validation checks)
  - SDK snippets for scoped subkeys and streaming reassembly
  - Sample route config that disables persistent KV caching and routes reranks to batch workers

Would you be available for a 30-minute engineering sync on Monday 10/26 at 11:00am PT? If so, we’ll send a calendar invite and include a short runbook for the session.

Best,
Irene
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx]
